A single signature object cannot express all conventions, so calling_convention is set to unknown.

Packet filename 'NamedEntryLookupInFormatList' understates behavior: on a lookup miss the function allocates a 0xb0-byte node, initializes it (SmallEntryStructInit arrays at +0x10/+0x38/+0x60/+0x88 + TextFormatStructInitializer) and appends it to the this[0..3] doubly-linked list, returning the new index.

Both are named TextFormatStructInitializer; bodies show the same 20-byte-block init pattern but different extents (0x00414D70 initializes through this+0xa8, 0x00414FE0 through this+0x58). They are likely two distinct text-format types, not one shared struct.

Labeled TrackNameDisplayIDLookup; the C shows a track-name to display-id table (AlbertPark..Indianapolis) with two id ranges selected by flag a3, but the id namespace (menu list ids?) is not provable from the C alone.

Labeled ConfigDirectoryPathRegistration; consistent with the C (path string defaults + flag dwords at +0xb8..+0xe8), but the ordering/semantics of the 22 string fields and the 0xbf800000 float at +0xe8 are inferred, not externally confirmed.

unresolved: StringCopyWithBufferRealloc target is ambiguous in the decompile: each call shows only the string argument, not the destination member, so the exact string-field offsets inside the initialized nodes cannot be locked down; it may write into the current object's string member or into a static scratch buffer.

The seven byte-identical functions 0x004218D0, 0x004218F0, 0x00421910, 0x00421930, 0x00421950, 0x00421970, 0x00421990 share the exact body (PathTrailingBackslashNormalizer + StringCopyWithBufferRealloc); whether they are distinct registration entry points or one function reached at seven addresses is undecidable from the C alone.

The -1 sentinel and the numeric ids produced by the name/team/track lookups (0x00415D90, 0x00417640, 0x00417AF0, 0x00417F60) are not tied to a known id namespace; the meaning of a3 (0/1) and the a4/a5 flag semantics are derived only from branch structure.
